newsitem.title: SPAIN: German suspected of aiding ETA arrested - Spain.
newsitem.headline: German suspected of aiding ETA arrested - Spain.

text.p: German police have arrested a German man accused of aiding the violent Basque separatist group ETA, Spanish Interior Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja said on Wednesday.

The suspect, named as Fritz Siemund, is believed to be one of four people who fled on Saturday from an ETA safe house in Madrid that was packed with weapons, officials said. An accidental explosion in the flat led neighbours to alert police who arrived minutes after the four escaped.

Mayor Oreja told a news conference Siemund was a suspected member of an ETA cell operating in the Spanish capital and believed to be behind past attacks in Madrid. But he said it was still unclear if Siemund had been directly involved in violence.
"Yesterday afternoon, a supposed member of the Madrid command, Fritz Siemund, was detained by German police," Mayor Oreja said.
ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) has killed some 800 people in a nearly 29-year campaign of violence for an independent Basque state.
Mayor Oreja said a German woman identified as Renate Heike Schubbert was believed to have fled the safe house with Siemund.
The case is a rare example of foreigners working with ETA inside Spain.
Mayor Oreja said he did not yet know if any charges had been presented against Siemund in a German court.
"It's clear we have charges against him...for belonging to Commando Madrid," he said, referring to the ETA cell.
He said he expected full judicial cooperation from Germany.
Asked whether Spain would seek Siemund's extradition, the minister replied: "We are going to look for instruments to bring this person to justice in one country or another."
Spanish state television quoted judicial sources as saying the government would not ask German authorities to hand over Siemund because Germany does not extradite its own nationals.
Mayor Oreja said he believed Siemund had fled Spain on Saturday after abandoning the flat in Madrid.

Police in the German city of Wiesbaden had set up surveillance on two apartments after Spain asked for German help in identifying and finding the two suspects. The police spotted Siemund on Monday afternoon going into his home.
He tried to escape and went to a lawyer's house where, after consultations, he surrendered to police, the minister said.
